Algebra I · Lesson 3.2

Zero and Negative Exponents

Solve this lesson →All lessons

3.1 kept the larger exponent on top of every quotient, and that restriction is now gone. Once the bottom exponent can be the larger one, the quotient rule's subtraction runs past zero, so x0x0 and x−3x−3 have to mean something. There is a second change. The base is a letter now, and a letter can be zero without looking like it.

Problem
A column lists powers of dd for some nonzero dd, and each entry is the one above it divided by dd. Reading down, the entries are d⋅d⋅dd⋅d⋅d, then d⋅dd⋅d, then dd. Take one more step down, which lands on d0d0. Enter its value.
Show a hint
  • Each step down divides by dd, and the last step is no different from the ones above it.
  • The entry above the one you want is dd itself, so the step is d÷dd÷d.
Show the full solution
Every step down the column divides by dd, including the last one. The entry above d0d0 is dd, so d0=d÷d=1.d0=d÷d=1​. The base cancels itself. Nothing about the step changed just because the exponent reached zero.
Problem
A table lists the value of t0t0 for t=13t=13, t=−9t=−9, t=0t=0 and t=50t=50. Check each value of tt against the zero exponent rule before you count. For how many of the four is t0t0 equal to 11?
Show a hint
  • The zero power needs a base that is not zero. Check each value of tt against that.
  • A negative base is still a nonzero base, so (−9)0=1(−9)0=1. Now test t=0t=0 against the condition.
Show the full solution
130130, (−9)0(−9)0 and 500500 are all 11, and 0000 has no value, so 33​ of the four are equal to 11. The rule a0=1a0=1 needs a nonzero base, and a negative base still counts as nonzero. Zero is left out because t0t0 comes from tntntntn​, which divides by zero when t=0t=0.
Key idea
The zero power. For any nonzero xx, x0=1.x0=1. Read a column of powers downward. Each step drops the exponent by one and divides the value by xx, so the step from x1x1 to x0x0 divides xx by itself, and 11 is the only place it can land. The nonzero condition is real work now. A numeral is visibly zero or visibly not, and you settle it by looking. A letter settles nothing until it gets a value, and if that value is 00 the step becomes 0÷00÷0, which is not a number. So x0=1x0=1 for every xx except 00, and 0000 has no value at all.

The column is one route to x0x0, and the quotient rule is the other. It reaches further than the column does, because subtracting exponents does not stop at zero. The next two problems run one fraction through both readings and then make the readings agree.

Problem
Simplify h2h8h8h2​ for nonzero hh by writing out the factors and cancelling. Nothing here needs the quotient rule. Enter what remains, typed like 1/y51/y5.
Show a hint
  • Two factors on top, eight on the bottom. Pair them off.
  • Each factor on top cancels one on the bottom. Count how many factors are left underneath.
Show the full solution
The two factors of hh on top cancel two of the eight underneath, which leaves 8−2=68−2=6 factors on the bottom and nothing but 11 on top. h2h8=1h6h8h2​=h61​​
Problem
Now read the same fraction h2h8h8h2​ through the quotient rule from 3.1, which subtracts the exponents. Nothing in that rule ever said the top exponent had to be the larger one. Enter the exponent it puts on hh.
Show a hint
  • The rule is xmxn=xm−nxnxm​=xm−n. Put 22 and 88 in and do the subtraction.
  • Subtract in the order the rule gives, so it is 2−82−8 and not 8−28−2. A negative result is fine as an exponent.
Show the full solution
The quotient rule subtracts the exponents whether or not the top one is larger. h2h8=h2−8=h−6h8h2​=h2−8=h−6 so the exponent is −6−6​. The last problem read the same fraction as 1h6h61​, and one fraction has one value, so h−6h−6 and 1h6h61​ are the same thing.
Key idea
Negative exponents. For any nonzero xx, x−n=1xn.x−n=xn1​. This is forced, not chosen. Cancelling h2h8h8h2​ by hand leaves 1h6h61​, the quotient rule reads the same fraction as h−6h−6, and one fraction has one value, so the two forms are the same number. A negative exponent is a reciprocal, not a negative number. x−4x−4 is positive whenever xx is, because it is 11 divided by a positive amount. What the minus sign does is put the factor under the bar.
Problem
Rewrite v−4v−4 with a positive exponent, then evaluate it at v=3v=3. Enter the value as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • A negative exponent puts the matching positive power under a 11.
  • So this is 1v4v41​. Now put 33 in for vv.
Show the full solution
A negative exponent is a reciprocal, so v−4=1v4v−4=v41​. At v=3v=3 that is 134=181.341​=811​​. A negative exponent puts the power under the bar and never turns the value negative, so −81−81 and −181−811​ are both wrong turns.
Problem
Simplify 1g−7g−71​ for nonzero gg, leaving no fraction bar and no negative exponent. Enter the result, typed like y5y5.
Show a hint
  • Rewrite the bottom first. What does g−7g−7 equal with a positive exponent?
  • The bottom becomes 1g7g71​, and dividing by a fraction multiplies by its reciprocal.
Show the full solution
The bottom is g−7=1g7g−7=g71​, so the whole thing is 11 divided by 1g7g71​, and dividing by a fraction multiplies by its reciprocal. 1g−7=g7g−71​=g7​ A factor with a negative exponent on the bottom moves up top and its exponent turns positive. The move runs both ways.
Key idea
Simplified means positive exponents. A finished answer carries no negative exponent, and getting there is one move run in whichever direction you need. x−n=1xn1x−n=xnx−n=xn1​x−n1​=xn A factor crosses the fraction bar and the sign of its exponent flips. The value does not change, only the way it is written, so you are free to do it at any point in a problem. Watch the word factor. Only the piece the exponent is written on crosses. Everything multiplied alongside it stays exactly where it is.

A monomial has a number out front and powers of letters after it, and an exponent written on one of those letters has nothing to do with the number. This is where the most common wrong answer of the chapter lives. The next two problems are built to make the difference impossible to argue with.

Problem
A student writes 5c−1=15c5c−1=5c1​. Test the claim the way 1.4 did, by picking a number. Take c=2c=2 and work out what 5c−15c−1 is really worth there. Enter that value as a fraction in lowest terms or an exact decimal.
Show a hint
  • The −1−1 is written on cc. Ask what it is attached to before you move anything.
  • 5c−15c−1 means 5⋅c−15⋅c−1, so the 55 is a separate factor sitting out front. Only c−1c−1 becomes a reciprocal.
Show the full solution
The exponent is written on cc alone, so 5c−1=5⋅1c=5c5c−1=5⋅c1​=c5​, and at c=2c=2 that is 52.25​​. The student's version gives 15⋅2=1105⋅21​=101​, which is 2525 times too small. The 55 never moves, because no exponent was ever written on it.
Problem
One pair of parentheses is the only difference between 7q−27q−2 and (7q)−2(7q)−2, and they are not the same expression. Rewrite (7q)−2(7q)−2 with no negative exponent. Enter the result, typed like 1/(3y4)1/(3y4).
Show a hint
  • In 7q−27q−2 the exponent is written on qq. In (7q)−2(7q)−2 the parentheses put the whole product 7q7q under it.
  • So the second one is 1(7q)2(7q)21​, and squaring a product squares both factors, the way 3.1's power of a product did.
Show the full solution
The exponent applies to the whole product 7q7q, so (7q)−2=1(7q)2=149q2.(7q)−2=(7q)21​=49q21​​. Without the parentheses, 7q−2=7q27q−2=q27​, which keeps the 77 upstairs. At q=2q=2, (7q)−2(7q)−2 is 11961961​ while 7q−27q−2 is 7447​, a factor of 343343 apart.
Key idea
A negative exponent moves only its own factor. kx−n=kxn(kx)−n=1knxnkx−n=xnk​(kx)−n=knxn1​ In kx−nkx−n the exponent is written on xx, so only x−nx−n becomes a reciprocal and the coefficient stays on top. That makes 2x−1=2x2x−1=x2​, not 12x2x1​. Those two differ by a factor of 44, which makes the error obvious the moment you put a number in. The parentheses in (kx)−n(kx)−n hand the whole product to the exponent, so the coefficient goes down and gets raised as well. No parentheses, no exponent on the coefficient, no movement.
Problem
Simplify (4z−3)−2(4z−3)−2 so that no exponent is negative. The outer −2−2 reaches the 44 as well as the z−3z−3, the way 3.1's power of a product did. Enter the result, typed like y5/9y5/9.
Show a hint
  • Handle the two factors inside separately. What is 4−24−2, and what is (z−3)−2(z−3)−2?
  • Power of a power multiplies the exponents, and (−3)×(−2)(−3)×(−2) is positive.
Show the full solution
The outer exponent applies to every factor inside the parentheses, so take the 44 and the z−3z−3 one at a time. Power of a power multiplies exponents and (−3)(−2)=6(−3)(−2)=6, so (z−3)−2=z6(z−3)−2=z6, while the coefficient gives 4−2=1164−2=161​. (4z−3)−2=z616(4z−3)−2=16z6​​ Leaving the 44 alone gives 4z64z6, and flipping the wrong way gives 16z6z616​.
Key idea
A negative power of a whole monomial. (kxm)−n=1knxmn(kxm)−n=knxmn1​ Nothing new is happening here. Power of a product from 3.1 sends the outer exponent to every factor inside, giving k−nx−mnk−nx−mn, and then each factor with a negative exponent crosses the bar. Power of a power multiplies exponents, so a negative inner exponent times a negative outer one comes out positive, which is why (4z−3)−2(4z−3)−2 puts z6z6 on top. The one thing that goes wrong is forgetting the coefficient is inside the parentheses too.
Problem
Simplify 12r318r1018r1012r3​ completely, with no negative exponent left. The coefficients and the powers of rr do not get the same treatment. Enter the result, typed like 3/(4y2)3/(4y2), with the whole denominator inside the parentheses.
Show a hint
  • Split it into a number part and an rr part. The numbers reduce, the exponents subtract.
  • The exponents give 3−103−10, which is negative. A factor with a negative exponent moves to the denominator, and its exponent turns positive there.
Show the full solution
The coefficients reduce, 1218=231812​=32​, and the exponents subtract, 3−10=−73−10=−7, so partway you have 23r−732​r−7. 23r−7=23⋅1r7=23r732​r−7=32​⋅r71​=3r72​​ Only the factor with the negative exponent moves to the denominator. The 2332​ has no negative exponent, so it stays where it is.
Problem
Simplify 20a4b645a9b645a9b620a4b6​ for nonzero aa and bb, leaving no negative exponent. One of the two letters disappears entirely, and the fact that it is nonzero is what lets that happen. Enter the result, typed like 5/(7y3)5/(7y3).
Show a hint
  • Three separate jobs. Reduce the numbers, subtract the aa exponents, subtract the bb exponents.
  • The bb exponents subtract to 00, and b0=1b0=1 because bb is not zero. A factor of 11 can be dropped.
Show the full solution
Reduce the coefficients, 2045=494520​=94​. Subtract on aa, 4−9=−54−9=−5. Subtract on bb, 6−6=06−6=0, and b0=1b0=1 since bb is nonzero, so the bb factors cancel and leave nothing behind. 49a−5=49a594​a−5=9a54​​ Only a−5a−5 moves to the denominator, since the 44 carries no exponent. Subtracting the other way gives a5a5 on top, which is the common miss.
Fun fact
The old word for exponent was index. John Wallis argued in 1656 that the index table ought to keep running below zero, and he wrote x−1x−1 for the reciprocal so one rule could cover the whole table. Newton took the notation up and it stuck.

Every exponent in this lesson was a whole number, positive, zero or negative, and the laws from 3.1 handled all of them without a single new rule. Nothing in those laws says an exponent has to be a whole number. 3.3 asks what x1/2x1/2 could mean, and the answer comes from the same place these did, whichever value keeps the laws working.

Practice these ideas

Practice
For nonzero kk, evaluate 8k0+(8k)08k0+(8k)0.
Show the solution
The first term is 8k0=8⋅1=88k0=8⋅1=8 and the second is (8k)0=1(8k)0=1, so the sum is 8+1=98+1=9​. Reading the first term as (8k)0(8k)0 instead gives 1+1=21+1=2, the common slip. There the exponent reaches only kk, so the 88 stays as a factor.
Practice
u0=1u0=1 holds for every value of uu but one. Enter the value it fails for.
Show the solution
u0=1u0=1 fails at u=0u=0​. Going from u1u1 down to u0u0 divides uu by itself, and at u=0u=0 that is 0÷00÷0, which is undefined. Every other base works, negative ones included.
Practice
Rewrite j−9j−9 with a positive exponent. Type it like 1/y41/y4.
Show the solution
A negative exponent means one over the matching positive power, so j−9=1j9j−9=j91​​. The minus sign moves the power to the bottom of a fraction. It does not make the value negative.
Practice
Evaluate w−3w−3 at w=2w=2. Enter it as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Rewriting gives w−3=1w3w−3=w31​, and at w=2w=2 that is 123=18231​=81​​. Treating the minus as a sign on the value gives −8−8, which is wrong in both size and sign.
Practice
Rewrite 6f−2f−26​ with no negative exponent. Type it like 3y43y4.
Show the solution
The f−2f−2 crosses the bar and the sign of its exponent flips, so 6f−2=6f2f−26​=6f2​. The 66 has no exponent written on it, so it does not move.
Practice
Simplify s5s13s13s5​ with no negative exponent left. Type it like 1/y41/y4.
Show the solution
Dividing powers of the same base subtracts the exponents, and 5−13=−85−13=−8, so the quotient is s−8=1s8s−8=s81​​. Cancelling gives the same result, since five of the thirteen factors in the denominator pair off with the five on top and eight stay below the bar.
Practice
Rewrite 10p−310p−3 with no negative exponent. Type it like 2/y52/y5.
Show the solution
The exponent sits on pp alone, so only p−3p−3 becomes a reciprocal and 10p−3=10p310p−3=p310​​. Dragging the 1010 down as well gives 110p310p31​, which is 100 times too small.
Practice
Evaluate 15e−215e−2 at e=3e=3. Enter it as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The exponent is written on ee alone, so 15e−2=15e215e−2=e215​, and at e=3e=3 that is 159=53915​=35​​. Moving the 1515 down too gives 11351351​, which is 225 times smaller.
Practice
Rewrite (3b)−3(3b)−3 with no negative exponent. Simplify the number too. Type it like 1/(2y4)1/(2y4).
Show the solution
(3b)−3=1(3b)3=127b3(3b)−3=(3b)31​=27b31​​. Because of the parentheses the exponent applies to both factors, so the 33 gets cubed along with the bb. Without them 3b−33b−3 means 3b3b33​ and the 33 stays on top.
Practice
Simplify (5c−2)−2(5c−2)−2 with no negative exponent left. Type it like y3/8y3/8.
Show the solution
Take the two factors inside separately. The coefficient gives 5−2=1255−2=251​, and power of a power multiplies exponents so (c−2)−2=c4(c−2)−2=c4, leaving c42525c4​​. Leaving the 55 untouched gives 5c45c4, which is 125 times too big.
Practice
Simplify (3h−6)(8h2)(3h−6)(8h2) with no negative exponent left. Type it like 5/y35/y3.
Show the solution
Coefficients multiply, 3⋅8=243⋅8=24, and exponents add, −6+2=−4−6+2=−4, so the product is 24h−4=24h424h−4=h424​​. Only the factor carrying the exponent crosses the bar, so the 2424 stays on top.
Practice
Simplify 30t−25t−95t−930t−2​ to a single term, then evaluate it at t=2t=2. Enter the value.
Show the solution
The coefficients divide, 30÷5=630÷5=6, and the exponents subtract, −2−(−9)=7−2−(−9)=7, so the term is 6t76t7. At t=2t=2 that is 6⋅27=6⋅128=7686⋅27=6⋅128=768​. Dropping the second minus gives −2−9=−11−2−9=−11 and the term 6t−116t−11, which at t=2t=2 is 3102410243​.
